column2: '1273781268']	Ford's CEO Says There's One C-Suite Job People Should Aim for	"The boss of Ford has some advice for up-and-coming executives: ditch CEO for CSCO.

column1: Speaking on an upcoming episode of "" Office Hours: Business Edition
column2: Jim Farley said people should aim for supply chain roles if they want to change the world and climb the corporate ladder.

column1: I would say of all the C-suite jobs that people should aspire to
column2: if you want to make a difference in our society
column3: I would pick one — supply chain
column4: the Ford CEO told host Monica Langley in the interview
column5: which is set to be released Wednesday morning.

column1: Farley said that at large companies such as Ford
column2: supply chain leaders must have a firm grasp of everything from technology to geopolitics.

column1: It's no surprise to me that Tim Cook and many of the CEOs in great companies today come from a supply chain background
column3: referring to the boss of Apple.

column1: No surprise at all to me
column2: because the leadership required to be world-class at supply chains is the same capability you need to run a company

column1: The role of chief supply chain officer
column3: has become increasingly important over the past few years. Some of the world's largest companies are now led by CEOs with a background in supply chains.

column1: Cook first joined Apple as a supply chain executive and played a vital role in building the tech giant's global manufacturing prowess. Mary Barra
column2: the CEO of Ford's crosstown rival GM
column3: also oversaw the company's global supply chain before becoming chief executive in 2014.

column1: Farley's comments come as the global auto industry grapples with a wave of supply chain disruptions.
The tariffs introduced by the Trump administration earlier this year have forced automakers
column2: which typically have factories and suppliers spread across the globe
column3: to reshuffle their supply chains and production plans.

column1: Ford said in its latest earnings that it expects the tariffs to cost it around $1 billion this year
column2: while rival GM has projected a tariff hit of $3.5-4.5 billion.

column1: Farley has regularly warned that not enough attention is being paid to manufacturing jobs in the US
column2: telling the ""Office Hours"" podcast that the country is in ""deep trouble"" compared to China.

column1: In an opinion piece for TIME in August
column2: the Ford CEO called for more vocational training programs to address workforce shortages in the construction and manufacturing industries.
Farley warned that the US was also far too dependent on other countries
column4: for vital materials like rare earths
column5: which are used to manufacture advanced magnets that are critical to the auto industry.

column1: China imposed restrictions on imports of rare earths earlier this year amid the trade war with the US
column2: sparking supply chain chaos at automakers and other manufacturers across the globe.
